correctness.rationale: Rayleigh variational formula makes N_G a norm. Vertex-disjoint edges give explicit flat faces; graphs of matching number one are exactly stars or K3 (mod isolates). Star norm is ℓ2/2. On K3 equality of Rayleigh/triangle inequalities with full Perron support forces the same edge coefficients by invertibility of the 3×3 edge-to-Ar map; one-edge support handled separately. For general graph a simple dominant Perron eigenvalue yields uniform quadratic perturbation remainder; ties or internal zero edges create first-order corners. Complex derivative is underlying real-linear as stated. Supplied finite checker is supporting evidence, not universal proof.
residual_risks: Only finite loopless undirected graphs and independent edge weights; zero excluded from smooth locus.

value.rationale: The matching obstruction produces a complete natural graph-theoretic criterion for strict convexity of numerical-radius norms; induced-leading-component gives a complete and computable differentiability locus including singular zero weights, with a sharp three-periodic shift corollary. Structural classification meaningful beyond finite numerical tests.

final_claim: For finite simple graphs and free real/complex edge weights, half the Perron adjacency root defines a strictly convex norm iff matching number one (star/triangle); real-Fréchet smoothness occurs iff the positive-support graph has a unique spectral leader inducing its vertices, with explicit derivative.
limitations: No loops, multi-edges, nonfree degree-coupled weights or infinite graph classification; Oxford VPN disconnected for Sharif.
